labels.description: The share of sales from products introduced in the past five years rolls forward from approximately 25% of 2024 sales to approximately 25% of 2025 sales, with the percentage unchanged.
labels.rationale: minor: the only change is a fiscal-year roll-forward (2024 to 2025) with the 25% figure and all other text identical.

labels.description: The foreign currency paragraph rolls forward from fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2025 with identical percentages (43% non-U.S., 23% Europe, 5% Western Hemisphere, 15% Asia-Pacific and Africa), the stale note that Egypt became highly inflationary beginning in fiscal Q4 2024 is dropped while Egypt stays on the list, and the subheading changes from Anti-bribery to Anti-corruption.
labels.rationale: minor: every change is a fiscal-year roll-forward, removal of a stale start-date qualifier with the same four highly inflationary jurisdictions still disclosed, or a relabeled subheading over unchanged FCPA and U.K. Bribery Act text.

labels.description: U.S. tariffs move from recently announced tariffs on China, Mexico and Canada to tariffs the U.S. government has imposed and/or announced on other jurisdictions, Russia is no longer named as the jurisdiction where patent holders' inventions may be exploited, data localization laws and data transfer restrictions are added as a protectionist policy exposure, and Middle East conflict is no longer described as rising.
labels.rationale: criterion 3 (tariffs go from announced to has imposed, and rising is dropped from the Middle East conflict) plus criterion 2 (Russia, China, Mexico and Canada are dropped as named jurisdictions) plus criterion 1 (data localization and data transfer restrictions are a newly disclosed exposure).

labels.description: Increasing use of and reliance on third parties is added as a driver of cyberattack exposure, and the AI sentence widens from increasing use of AI to increasing use of AI and other emerging technology.
labels.rationale: criterion 1 (third-party reliance is newly disclosed as a factor increasing breach risk) plus criterion 3 (scope of the technology risk widened beyond AI to other emerging technology).

labels.description: New risk that the Orthopaedics separation announced in October 2025, targeted for completion 18 to 24 months after announcement, may be delayed, not completed on the contemplated terms or at all, or fail to achieve expected results, given conditions such as works council consultations, final Board approval and regulatory approvals.

New risk that the planned Orthopaedics separation will require significant expenses and that the Company may not realize the full strategic and financial benefits expected from it, since those benefits rest on assumptions that may prove incorrect.

New risk that the trading price of the Company's common stock may fluctuate significantly and be more volatile around the planned Orthopaedics separation, with its post-separation market value possibly lower than before.
